content:
Pain and stiffness can mean sitting for long periods.

This guide covers pressure cushions and skin care. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Why pressure matters

Pressure reduces blood flow to skin, which can lead to pressure ulcers.

Cushions

  • Foam, gel or air cushions.
  • Get assessed for the right type.

Other steps

  • Change position regularly.
  • Check skin daily.
  • Eat and drink well.

Making a home work harder for you

  • A chair at the right height.
  • Footstool if needed.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Where do I get one?

Ask your GP, community nurse or OT.

What should I look for on skin?

Redness or discolouration that does not fade.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: Pressure ulcers (pressure sores)
